strengths: Addresses a well-motivated gap: SFT is ill-suited for 3D layout generation since no single ground-truth layout exists, and the paper proposes RL as an alternative learning paradigm.
The three-component reward design (format, physics-based, rendering-based) is a reasonable way to provide dense, structured feedback for layout generation.
Ablation studies (Table 2) and multi-turn vs. single-step comparisons (Table 3) are included, isolating the contribution of each reward term and refinement depth.
The multi-turn refinement + GRPO framing, treating trajectories as groups for relative reward comparison, is a sensible adaptation of GRPO to an iterative generation setting.
Clear articulation of the pipeline (Figure 1) makes the overall system easy to follow conceptually.
weaknesses: No comparison against any external/prior baseline methods discussed at length in related work (LayoutGPT, I-Design, LayoutVLM, LayoutDreamer); all quantitative comparisons are purely internal ablations (RL vs. no-RL, reward-component removal), making it impossible to judge whether MetaSpatial actually advances the state of the art.

Evaluation relies on GPT-4o both as the training reward signal and as the primary quality metric, creating a circular/self-reinforcing evaluation loop; no independent human evaluation or other automated metric is used to validate that GPT-4o scores correlate with actual layout quality.

Absolute performance after training remains weak (e.g., 76.2% constraint violation ratio and 13.7% collision ratio for the best 7B model, GPT-4o score of only 0.58/1.0), which undercuts the paper's claims of producing 'physically plausible' and 'coherent' scenes; this tension between claimed success and reported numbers is not discussed.

Dataset description is extremely sparse: no information on dataset size, source, scene diversity, room types, or how many training/test scenes were used; also unclear how 'ground-truth' object counts are obtained given the paper's core claim that no ground truth exists for layouts.
No statistical significance analysis, variance across seeds, or confidence intervals are reported; all results appear to be single runs.

Reproducibility is compromised: the code/data link in the abstract is empty, and important hyperparameters (e.g., λ weights beyond the fixed reward formula, γ decay factor value, GRPO clipping details, number of GRPO groups G) are not fully specified or justified.
The 'Overall' metric in Table 1 is not defined anywhere in the text, making it impossible to verify how it is computed from the other four metrics.

The abstract's claim of enabling 'real-time' 3D scene generation is inconsistent with a pipeline that requires Blender rendering and GPT-4o API calls for every refinement step, which would be costly and slow; no latency/throughput analysis is provided.
The introduction and framework overview are repeated almost verbatim across the abstract, introduction, and Section 2.2, leading to redundancy without adding new information.
Minor writing issues (e.g., 'RL s enables' typo) and lack of detail on how physics/format rules were validated for correctness reduce overall polish.
